In my recent question about free will vs. determinism, an issue that commonly came up was that determinism seems very classical (in the physics sense). People who are aware of quantum randomness conclude that because it's random, it's not deterministic (fairly tautologically true) and therefore we have free will (wat).

Going to an analogy of a game, I think everyone would a agree that playing a simple game like Candy Land with a pre generated list of spins would be classically deterministic and you'd have no free will within the game. If instead you rolled a die or spun a spinner to determine your next move, it wouldn't be deterministic, but the perspective of the player is similarly lacking any free will. You're a slave to the random. This is similar to the quantum physics reality we seem to have now. I propose a term to describe this but will first cover the last case for completeness. A final version could allocate you with resources when you land on certain spaces and you'd be able to spend them to move from one space to another. Here we finally see free will. Both of these last two are non-deterministic but they're very different and I feel the first two are much more similar from a player perspective.

I think the term should capture this similarity to determinism while still indicating the randomness. I propose stochastism. This is from the adjective stochastic which means: "randomly determined; having a random probability distribution or pattern that may be analyzed statistically but may not be predicted precisely."
I'm thinking I should coin a term

Don't take coining a term lightly. There are probably lots of 2-3 word combinations that describe what you need ("pseudo-free-will" or "illusion of choice" perhaps?). When you try to condense something to single word, you probably only make it harder for others and yourself to understand (you don't get any indication about what "stochastism" is when you just see the word). Short descriptions for things should grow organically: people only notice after a LONG discussion about something, that this something occurs everywhere, and because they have to refer to it frequently, that it needs to have a shorter identifier.

free will vs. determinism: I agree that not determinism does not imply free will. So it doesn't make sense to put these at opposite ends of each other. So I'm also uncomfortable having something between them like "stochastism". Also I'm not even sure free will exist, because I don't know any prove of it.

Chess could be the final game in you analogy: you are unfree in a sense that a good opponent forces you to loose, but you feel very free, because no randomness is involved in the rules. So there is probably also a difference between constraints to freedom that are universe-given and constraints that someone intentionally put in place to screw you.

The analogy between universe and games doesn't feel right: it suggests you can look at the universe the same way you can look at a game, from an "outside view". I think we are the pieces, not the players.
